A provider written outside the DbLive repository is not supported.

### 11.3 `DeployParameters` (record, namespace `DbLive`)

| Property | `new()` default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateDbIfNotExists` | `false` | Create the database if missing (SQL Server connects to `master`, PostgreSQL to `postgres`; needs permission). Off, a missing database fails the deployment with `DatabaseNotFoundException` before anything runs (Section 17). Only for local and test databases (rule 18). |
| `DeployMigrations` | `true` | Apply pending migrations. |
| `DeployCode` | `true` | Deploy changed code files. |
| `DeployBreaking` | `false` | Run the breaking phase (Section 5.5): the guard, the breaking scripts of the Code folder, the pending breaking scripts of migrations. |
| `RepairMigrationChecksums` | `false` | Accept edited applied migrations by updating stored hashes. |

Presets (each access returns a new instance; adjust with `with { ... }`):

| Preset | CreateDb | Migrations | Code | Breaking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DeployParameters.Default` | no | yes | yes | no |
| `DeployParameters.Breaking` | no | no | no | yes |

Even with all flags off, a deployment still performs: ProjectId validation, self-deployment, settings validation, the applied versions check (Section 5.2), checksum validation, saving migration items, BeforeDeploy and AfterDeploy. There is no flag for the SQL tests: a deployment never runs them (Section 8.2).

### 11.4 `IDbLiveTester` (namespace `DbLive.Testing`)

```csharp
Task RunAllTestsAsync();   // all SQL tests in parallel, results in dblive.unit_test_run; throws UnitTestsFailedException (Section 8.2)
Task<TestRunResult> RunTestAsync(Action<string> writeLine, string relativePath);   // one test, used by [SqlFact]
// TestRunResult (DbLive.Testing): IsSuccess, ErrorMessage, Exception; the output of the test goes to writeLine
```

`RunAllTestsAsync` checks the database first (DbLive tables, the minimum DbLive version, ProjectId, isolation levels; Section 8.2). `RunTestAsync` does not check and does not store the result: the `[SqlFact]` fixture has just deployed the database.

### 11.5 `IDbLiveFixtureBuilder` (namespace `DbLive`) and the fixture builders

```csharp
public interface IDbLiveFixtureBuilder
{
    Task<DbLiveBuilder> GetBuilderAsync();   // once per fixture: provider, connection string of a new database, project
    Assembly GetProjectAssembly();           // the SQL project assembly; [SqlFact] discovery reads the tests from it
}
```

The caller owns the builder it gets and disposes it at the end, after the drop of the database: `DbLiveTestFixture` in its `DisposeAsync`, `DeploymentTest` at the end of `DeployAsync`. `GetBuilderAsync` returns a new builder on every call, never a shared one.

Ready-made implementations; each takes the SQL project assembly and gives every `GetBuilderAsync` call a new random database name (`DbLive--<guid>` on SQL Server, `dblive--<guid>` on PostgreSQL). They do not create the database: the fixture's deployment does (`CreateDbIfNotExists = true`).

| Class | Package / namespace | Database |
|---|---|---|
| `MsSqlFixtureBuilder(Assembly project, string connectionString)` | `DbLive.MSSQL` / `DbLive.MSSQL` | On the server of `connectionString`; its database name is replaced. |
| `PostgreSqlFixtureBuilder(Assembly project, string connectionString)` | `DbLive.PostgreSQL` / `DbLive.PostgreSQL` | Same, PostgreSQL. |
| `MsSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(Assembly project)`, `MsSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(Assembly project, string image)` | `DbLive.Testcontainers.MSSQL` / `DbLive.MSSQL` | SQL Server in Docker; without `image`: `mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest`, SQL Server 2025 with its updates. |
| `PostgreSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(Assembly project)`, `PostgreSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(Assembly project, string image)` | `DbLive.Testcontainers.PostgreSQL` / `DbLive.PostgreSQL` | PostgreSQL in Docker; without `image`: `postgres:18`, a major version, with its minor releases. |

The default image is not a public constant. A new major version of the database engine in it is a breaking change and comes only in a major DbLive release; an update within the same major version is not ([Versioning](https://zacoders.github.io/DbLive/versioning/)). Pass the image to stay on one version.

Container builders: one container per image per test process, started by the first `GetBuilderAsync` call; concurrent calls wait for that start and share the container. A failed start is not retried: every fixture of the run fails with its exception (Docker not running, image not found). The container is not stopped by DbLive; the Testcontainers resource reaper removes it when the test process ends.

---

## 12. Deployment pipeline (exact order of `DeployAsync`)

1. **Load the project**, before anything touches the server: `settings.json` and the isolation levels it sets, which the provider must support; then every file the deployment runs, whatever the `DeployParameters`: migrations and their item settings (with the isolation levels they set, which the provider must support), code, the breaking scripts of the Code folder, BeforeDeploy and AfterDeploy (not the SQL tests). The checks of Sections 4 and 5.1 fail here (`FilesOutsideProjectFoldersException`, `ScriptPathsDifferOnlyByCaseException`, `UndoNotSupportedException` and other file name errors, item settings errors), and so does a file that cannot be read or is not UTF-8 (`FileNotUtf8Exception`, Section 4). Such an error creates no database and leaves the `dblive` tables as they were: an older DbLive can still deploy the database (Section 18.8). The steps after this one read no project file.
2. (internal option) drop and recreate the database.
3. `CreateDbIfNotExists` (off by default): create the database if missing. Off: check that the database exists, otherwise `DatabaseNotFoundException` (Section 17).
4. **ProjectId check** (Section 14): a database whose stored ProjectId differs fails with `ProjectIdMismatchException` before anything changes, also before the self-deployment.
5. **Self-deployment** (transaction, Serializable): check the minimum DbLive version the database requires (`DatabaseRequiresNewerDbLiveException` before any change, Section 15), create or upgrade the `dblive` schema, store the minimum version of this DbLive. Then the ProjectId is stored in a database that has none (Section 14).
6. Begin the deployment transaction if `TransactionWrapLevel` is `Deployment`.
7. **Applied versions check** (Section 5.2): every migration version applied to the database must be in the project, otherwise `DatabaseAheadOfProjectException`, before any script of the project runs.
8. **Checksum validation** of applied migration items (Section 5.4).
9. **Save migration items** to `dblive.migration`.
10. **BeforeDeploy** folder.
11. **Migrations**, if `DeployMigrations`.
12. **Code**, if `DeployCode`; then the rows of files missing from the project are marked `removed` (Section 6).
13. **Breaking**, if `DeployBreaking` (Section 5.5): guard (`CodeNotDeployedException` unless every code file is deployed with its current content), then every breaking script of the Code folder, then the pending breaking scripts of migrations.
14. **AfterDeploy** folder.
15. Commit the deployment transaction (if any).

The SQL tests are not a step of the deployment: they run in xUnit, or with `IDbLiveTester.RunAllTestsAsync()` (Section 8.2).

---

## 13. xUnit integration (`DbLive.xunit`, xUnit v2)

SQL tests run like ordinary C# unit tests: the fixture builds a temporary database from the project scripts (in a Docker container or on a local server, with a random name), the tests run against it, and the database is dropped at the end. No shared test database is needed, and every developer machine and CI run starts from the same database.

Test project packages: `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`, `xunit` (2.x), `xunit.runner.visualstudio`, `DbLive.xunit`, and `DbLive.Testcontainers.MSSQL` or `DbLive.Testcontainers.PostgreSQL` (a test database in Docker; brings the provider and Testcontainers). Without Docker: the provider package instead. Reference the SQL project.

### 13.1 Fixture builder

The fixture gets its database from an `IDbLiveFixtureBuilder` (Section 11.5). Use a ready-made one; do not write a builder class unless the database needs a setup they do not cover:

```csharp
using DbLive.MSSQL;
using System.Reflection;

new MsSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(typeof(MyDbMarker).Assembly)                 // SQL Server in Docker
new MsSqlFixtureBuilder(typeof(MyDbMarker).Assembly,
    "Server=localhost;Database=master;Trusted_Connection=True;TrustServerCertificate=True;")   // a local server

// PostgreSQL (using DbLive.PostgreSQL):
new PostgreSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(typeof(MyDbMarker).Assembly)            // postgres:18 in Docker
new PostgreSqlFixtureBuilder(typeof(MyDbMarker).Assembly, "Host=localhost;Username=postgres;Password=...")
```

Every fixture gets a new database with a random name on that server, so test classes that xUnit runs in parallel never share one. A custom builder implements both members of `IDbLiveFixtureBuilder` (namespace `DbLive`): `GetBuilderAsync()` returns `new DbLiveBuilder().SqlServer().SetDbConnection(<connection string with a new database name>).SetProject(<assembly>)`, a new builder on every call (its caller disposes it, Section 11.5), `GetProjectAssembly()` returns the same assembly.

### 13.2 Every SQL test as its own xUnit test: `[SqlFact]`

```csharp
using DbLive.MSSQL;
using DbLive.Testing;
using DbLive.xunit;
using Xunit;
using Xunit.Abstractions;

// Must derive from DbLiveTestFixture and have a public parameterless constructor.
public class MyDbTestFixture()
    : DbLiveTestFixture(new MsSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(typeof(MyDbMarker).Assembly), dropDatabaseOnComplete: true);

public class SqlTests(ITestOutputHelper output, MyDbTestFixture fixture)
    : IClassFixture<MyDbTestFixture>
{
    [SqlFact(TestFixture = typeof(MyDbTestFixture))]
    public async Task Sql(string testFileRelativePath)
    {
        TestRunResult result = await fixture.Tester.RunTestAsync(output.WriteLine, testFileRelativePath);
        Assert.True(result.IsSuccess, result.ErrorMessage);
    }
}
```

- Discovery creates one test case per SQL test file; the display name is the relative path and "go to source" opens the `.sql` file at `<ProjectDir>/<DbLiveScriptsFolder>/<relative path>`, from the assembly metadata (Section 3.1) of the fixture builder's `GetProjectAssembly()`; `Scripts` when `DbLiveScriptsFolder` is missing. Without the `ProjectDir` metadata the tests are still discovered and run, only "go to source" does not open the `.sql` file.
- Discovery reads tests from the SQL project's dll (`SetProject`), so a new test file appears after a build; Test Explorer and `dotnet test` build before running.
- The fixture deploys once per test class (migrations, code and breaking; no tests) into a fresh database, then drops it if `dropDatabaseOnComplete`.
- An invalid `TestFixture` type produces a failing test case that explains the fix.
- An error of the project found while discovery reads the tests (`ScriptsNotEmbeddedException`, `FilesOutsideProjectFoldersException` and the other checks of Section 4, an invalid `settings.json`) produces one failing test case named after the test method: xUnit reports "Exception during discovery" with the exception, and `dotnet test` fails.

### 13.3 Deployment test: `[SqlDeployFact]`

```csharp
using DbLive.MSSQL;
using DbLive.xunit;
using Xunit.Abstractions;

public class DeploymentTests(ITestOutputHelper output)
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Deploys the project to an empty database as production does, in three deployments:
    /// 1. migrations and code, then the SQL tests;
    /// 2. the breaking phase, then the SQL tests again;
    /// 3. the breaking phase once more, which must not change the schema.
    /// Then drops the database.
    /// </summary>
    [SqlDeployFact]
    public Task ReleaseDeploys() => new DeploymentTest(
        fixtureBuilder: new MsSqlContainerFixtureBuilder(typeof(MyDbMarker).Assembly),
        dropDatabaseOnComplete: true).DeployAsync(output);
}
```

`[SqlDeployFact]` is a plain xUnit fact (a `FactAttribute` without parameters); the test is one case. `DeploymentTest` (namespace `DbLive.xunit`) is not an xUnit fixture: the test creates it with `new`, and the test class implements no `IAsyncLifetime`. `DeploymentTest.DeployAsync(output)` gets a new database from the fixture builder, deploys it, drops it when `dropDatabaseOnComplete` is true (also when the deployment fails; an error of the drop goes to the test output and does not replace the error of the deployment), and disposes the builder. It deploys to the fresh database as production does, in three deployments:

1. Migrations and code (the flags of `DeployParameters.Default`, with `CreateDbIfNotExists`: the database is new), then all SQL tests (`RunAllTestsAsync`). The release is deployed, its breaking changes are not: old application instances still run.
2. `DeployParameters.Breaking`: the breaking phase, then all SQL tests again. The breaking phase guard must pass after a normal deployment. The breaking script of every migration runs once, with its own settings file.
3. `DeployParameters.Breaking` once more: every breaking script of the Code folder runs again (catches a non-idempotent one) and BeforeDeploy/AfterDeploy scripts run a third time; migration breaking scripts are already applied and do not run. The schema must not change.

A deployment where every migration runs once, in one run with the breaking phase, followed by every SQL test on that data, is what the `[SqlFact]` fixture does (Section 13.2): keep both. Limit: on a fresh database an old version such as `_v1` never existed, so dropping an `_v1` that really exists is not tested (it needs the build of the previous release). Keep this test in CI.

Schema check. A script that runs without an error is not enough: the deployment test reads the schema from the catalog (`sys.*` views, `pg_catalog`) before and after the last deployment, `DeployParameters.Breaking` once more, in which the breaking scripts of the Code folder, BeforeDeploy and AfterDeploy run again. A difference fails the case with `SchemaChangedException` (namespace `DbLive.Testing`); its message lists the differences.

- Compared: schemas; tables (partitioning, unlogged, system versioning); columns (type with length/precision/scale, nullability, default, identity seed and increment, computed or generated expression, collation); primary keys, unique, foreign key (columns, referenced table, actions, disabled/not trusted) and check constraints, PostgreSQL exclusion constraints; indexes (key columns and their order, included columns, filter, unique, index type, disabled); views (also PostgreSQL materialized views), functions, procedures and triggers (definition text, disabled); user types (SQL Server alias and table types; PostgreSQL enums, domains, composite and range types); sequences (options); SQL Server synonyms and database DDL triggers; PostgreSQL extensions (version, schema) and event triggers.
- Not compared: DbLive's own schema `dblive`; data (a breaking script whose second run deletes more rows passes); object ids; column order; names that SQL Server generates for unnamed constraints (`DF__Person__Phone__3A81B327`): such a default belongs to its column, a primary key to its table, an unnamed unique, foreign key or check constraint is identified by its table and definition; current identity and sequence values; statistics; permissions; extended properties and comments; objects that belong to a PostgreSQL extension; physical options (fill factor, compression, filegroup, partition scheme).
- Definitions are compared as text in the engine's own form. The text of views, functions, procedures and triggers is compared with whitespace collapsed; on SQL Server `create or alter` and `alter` count as `create` (the server stores them so). PostgreSQL names are compared as they are: the names it generates (`person_pkey`, `person_age_check`) depend only on the table and columns.
- Requires SQL Server 2017 or later (`string_agg`, `concat_ws`; every SQL Server Docker image qualifies) or PostgreSQL 12 or later. Production deployments never read the snapshot.

Failure message (one line per object; `missing`: in the earlier schema only, `extra`: in the later one only, `changed` with `was`/`now`; the objects of a missing or extra table are counted on its line):

A breaking script of the Code folder whose second run drops more than the first one, typically because it checks a condition on an object it drops itself:

```
DbLive.Testing.SchemaChangedException : Deployment test: a second breaking deployment changed the schema. The breaking scripts of the Code folder and the BeforeDeploy/AfterDeploy scripts run again on it and must not change the schema:
  missing check constraint dbo.Person.CK_Person_Name: check ([Name]<>'')
  missing index dbo.Person.IX_Person_Name: nonclustered (Name asc)
  missing table dbo.PersonPhones (with 3 columns, 1 primary key)
```

---

## 14. ProjectId

- Optional but recommended (rule 17) `"ProjectId"` in `settings.json`, max 128 characters (a longer one fails every deployment and test run with `ProjectIdMismatchException`), case-insensitive, stored lowercase in `dblive.version.project_id`.
- Not set, empty or whitespace: no validation, and every deployment logs a warning: `ProjectId is not set in settings.json, so nothing stops this project from being deployed to the database of another project. ...` `RunAllTestsAsync` does not log it.
- Set, and the database has no stored value: the value is stored right after the self-deployment (first deployment binds the database).
- Set, and the stored value differs: `ProjectIdMismatchException`, nothing is deployed. The check runs before the self-deployment, so a newer DbLive pointed at the database of another project does not upgrade its `dblive` tables either.
- Before the SQL tests (`RunAllTestsAsync`, Section 8.2) the value is only compared, never stored: a database with another value or with none fails with `ProjectIdMismatchException` and no test runs. A deployment of the project stores the value, so this stops only tests run against a database the project was not deployed to.
- `settings.json` is the same file for every environment, so the value identifies the **project**, not the environment. It protects against pointing project A's deployer at project B's database (a common mistake when several services share one server). It does not distinguish staging from production.
- To rebind a database on purpose: `update dblive.version set project_id = null;` then deploy.

---

## 15. DbLive's own schema (`dblive`)

Created and upgraded automatically on every deployment. Same tables in both providers.

| Table | Content |
|---|---|
| `dblive.version` | One row: internal schema version (`version`, the last self-migration), `project_id`, `min_dblive_lib_version` (below). |
| `dblive.migration` | One row per `(version, item_type)`: `item_type` (`migration`/`breaking`/`migration.settings`/`breaking.settings`, following the file names; databases deployed by older DbLive versions have their `settings` rows renamed to `migration.settings` automatically), `name`, `relative_path`, `status` (`none`/`applied`), `content_hash`, `created_utc`, `applied_utc`, `execution_time_ms`, `error`. No script content: the project is the source of the scripts. |
| `dblive.code` | One row per code file and per breaking script of the Code folder: `relative_path`, `item_type` (`code`/`breaking`; existing rows of older databases become `code`), `status` (`applied`/`error`, or `removed` for a file no longer in the project, Section 6), `content_hash`, `applied_utc` (last execution), `verified_utc` (last `[hash match]` of a code file, or when the file was found missing), `execution_time_ms`, `error`. A breaking script's row is written by each breaking deployment (Section 6.1). |
| `dblive.unit_test_run` | Last result per test file: `relative_path`, `pass`, `error`, `run_utc`, `execution_time_ms`. |
| `dblive.folder_items` | Last run per BeforeDeploy/AfterDeploy file. |

`error` of a code file or a breaking script of the Code folder holds the error of the server, without stack traces (they are in the exception and the log). SQL Server: `SQL Server error:`, then for each error `Msg <number>, Level <level>, State <state>, Line <line in the GO batch>`, the message, and `Procedure: <name>` when the error is in a procedure, view, function or trigger. PostgreSQL: `PostgreSQL error:`, then `Severity`, `SqlState`, `Message`, `Position`, `InternalQuery`, `Where`, `Routine`. An error without the details of the server stores the message of the exception. `error` of a test holds its failure message (Section 8.3). On SQL Server the column is `nvarchar(4000)`: a longer text is cut to 4000 characters and ends with `... [truncated]`, the full error is in the exception and the log. On PostgreSQL it is `text`, never cut.

Permissions of the deployment login on SQL Server: `db_ddladmin`, `db_datareader` and `db_datawriter` in the database are enough for everything DbLive does itself (self-migrations, migrations, code, breaking phase, BeforeDeploy/AfterDeploy, the `dblive` tables), also when the schema `dblive` belongs to another user, such as `dbo` after an administrator or DbLive 1.5 deployed the database first. `db_owner` is not needed. DbLive creates no object that needs a `grant`: it passes lists of file paths to its queries in an xml parameter and a temporary table. The scripts of the project need the permissions of their statements: a `grant` needs a permission that `db_ddladmin` does not give. `CreateDbIfNotExists = true` needs the server permission to create a database.

`relative_path` is relative to the scripts root, uses `/` on every OS and is stored in lower case (`code/dbo/getuser.sql`), so a file is identified ignoring case on SQL Server with any collation and on PostgreSQL. DbLive lower-cases the paths itself (.NET `ToLowerInvariant()`), the same on every database, collation and locale; to find the row of a file, compare with its path in lower case: `'code/dbo/getuser.sql'`. Databases deployed by older DbLive versions are converted automatically: `\` is replaced with `/` and paths are lower-cased with the database's `lower()` (on PostgreSQL with the `C` locale it lower-cases only ASCII letters, so a code file with other capital letters in its path runs once more after the upgrade); when one file has several rows (deployed from Windows and Linux, or renamed only by case on PostgreSQL or a case-sensitive collation), the latest row is kept. Logs and exceptions show the real path of the file. The one exception is the log line `Code files removed from the project, marked as removed in dblive.code: <paths>`: it shows the stored lower-case paths, because the files are no longer in the project and their real paths are not known.

Databases deployed by DbLive versions that had undo scripts are converted automatically too: the rows of `undo` and `undo.settings` items are deleted, and so are the rows with status `reverted` (a version that was rolled back is not applied: the next deployment records its items again and runs its migration if the project has it); the column `dblive.migration.content`, which held only undo scripts, is dropped.

`dblive.version.min_dblive_lib_version` is the oldest DbLive version that can deploy the database (`major.minor.patch`). A newer DbLive can store in the `dblive` tables what an older one cannot read or understands differently, with a self-migration or with its code alone. Each DbLive version has a minimum compatible version: the version of the latest such change it contains. Every deployment raises the stored value to it and never lowers it; it is written at the start of the deployment, in the self-deployment transaction, after the project is loaded: a deployment that fails on an error in its project files does not write it (Section 12, step 1). Before it changes anything, every deployment, and `RunAllTestsAsync` (Section 8.2), fails with `DatabaseRequiresNewerDbLiveException` when the stored value is above the minimum compatible version of the running DbLive: a newer DbLive has changed the tables in a way this one cannot read. A release that raises its minimum compatible version says in its release notes that older DbLive versions can no longer deploy the database. An older DbLive that the stored value allows deploys the database even when a newer DbLive has applied self-migrations it does not have: a self-migration that did not raise the minimum only adds what the older code does not see. The self-migration version is not lowered. DbLive before 2.0.0 does not check the value.

Diagnostic queries:

```sql
-- applied versions and their state
select version, item_type, status, applied_utc, relative_path from dblive.migration order by version, item_type;
-- code files that failed
select relative_path, error from dblive.code where status = 'error';
-- failed tests of the last RunAllTestsAsync() run ([SqlFact] tests are not stored)
select relative_path, error from dblive.unit_test_run where pass = 0;   -- PostgreSQL: where not pass
```

---

## 16. Provider differences

| Topic | SQL Server (`DbLive.MSSQL`) | PostgreSQL (`DbLive.PostgreSQL`) |
|---|---|---|
| Script execution | SMO `ServerConnection`: `GO` batch separators supported (except in test files) | Whole file sent as one command; no `GO`. A file with several statements runs as one implicit transaction: it fails or succeeds as a whole, also a code file or a script with `TransactionWrapLevel: None`; several `update`s in one file commit together. `commit` inside a `do` block or a procedure works only when the `do`/`call` is alone in a file with `TransactionWrapLevel: None` (comments are fine); otherwise `2D000: invalid transaction termination` |
| Test files | One batch, no `GO` | Normal multi-statement script |
| Create/drop database | via `master` | via `postgres` database |
| `Snapshot` isolation | Supported (`ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION ON` required) | Not supported: deployment fails at start, in `settings.json` or in an item settings file |
| Statements that cannot run in a transaction | `ALTER DATABASE`, full-text DDL, online index with long locks: an item settings file (`<version>.migration.settings.json` or `.breaking.settings.json`) with `TransactionWrapLevel: None` | `CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `VACUUM`: item settings file with `TransactionWrapLevel: None`, and keep the statement alone in its file (a multi-statement file runs as one implicit transaction: two `create index concurrently` in one file fail with `25001`, and the first index is left invalid) |
| Re-runnable code | `create or alter` | `create or replace`; `drop function if exists f(args)` before `create` when the signature or return type changes |
| Assert column | `select assert = 'rows'` or `select 'rows' as assert` | `select 'rows' as assert` |
| Error details | Msg number, level, state, line in batch, procedure | SqlState, severity, position, where |
| An error in the deployment transaction (`TransactionWrapLevel: Deployment`) | Most errors leave the transaction open, and a failed code file is retried. A run-time error with `XACT_ABORT ON`, a failed conversion and a deadlock roll it back: the file is not retried | Aborts the transaction. A code file runs under a savepoint, and the rollback to it lets the file be retried |

---

## 17. Exceptions: cause and fix

| Exception / message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ScriptsNotEmbeddedException: Assembly '<name>' has no embedded DbLive scripts` | `SetProject` got an assembly without `DbLive/` resources: the `.csproj` of the SQL project does not set `DbLiveScriptsFolder` or names another folder, the project does not reference a DbLive package (a project with only scripts needs `DbLive`), or it is the wrong assembly (for example the deployer instead of the SQL project in layout B) | Add `<DbLiveScriptsFolder>Scripts</DbLiveScriptsFolder>` (Section 3.1), `dotnet add package DbLive` in the SQL project, or pass the SQL project's assembly |
| Build error: `The DbLive package embeds the scripts of the 'Scripts' folder named by <DbLiveScriptsFolder> in the assembly, and <project>.csproj embeds N DbLive script(s) too. Remove the DbLive block from <project>.csproj ...` | The `.csproj` sets `DbLiveScriptsFolder` and embeds the scripts itself as well (Section 3.1) | Remove the `EmbeddedResource` with `LogicalName="DbLive/..."` and the `ProjectDir` `AssemblyAttribute`; or remove `DbLiveScriptsFolder` to keep embedding the scripts in the `.csproj` |
| `DirectoryNotFoundException: Scripts folder '<path>' not found.` | `SetScriptsFolder` got a folder that does not exist; a relative path is resolved against the current directory | Pass the right path |
| `[SqlFact]` test: "Go to source" does not open the `.sql` file | The SQL project's assembly lacks the `ProjectDir` metadata: it embeds the scripts in its `.csproj` (without `DbLiveScriptsFolder`) without the metadata | Add the `ProjectDir` `AssemblyMetadata` item, and `DbLiveScriptsFolder` for a folder other than `Scripts` (Section 3.1) |
| `JsonException` reading `settings.json` | Wrong case, unknown key, or trailing comma | Section 9.1 |
| `DatabaseNotFoundException: Database '<name>' does not exist on server '<server>'. ...` | The database of the connection string does not exist: `DeployAsync` with `CreateDbIfNotExists` off (the default, also in `DeployParameters.Default`), or `RunAllTestsAsync`. Nothing ran | Check the database name in the connection string. Create the database, or for a local or test database deploy with `DeployParameters.Default with { CreateDbIfNotExists = true }` |
| SQL Server: `SqlException: Cannot open database "<name>" requested by the login. The login failed.` (error 4060) | The database exists, but the login has no user in it. When the login cannot see the database list in `master` (no access to `master`, or no `VIEW ANY DATABASE`), DbLive cannot tell this from a missing database and also gives this error | Grant the login access to the database, or check the database name |
| `ProjectIdMismatchException` | Wrong database, or `ProjectId` changed. Before the SQL tests also a database without a stored ProjectId. Also a `ProjectId` longer than 128 characters | Check the connection string; rebind deliberately (Section 14); deploy the project before running the tests |
| `MigrationChecksumMismatchException` | An applied migration/breaking file was edited | Revert the file and add a new migration; or `RepairMigrationChecksums = true` if the database already matches |
| `DatabaseAheadOfProjectException: The database has applied migration versions that the project does not have: ...` | The database has applied versions this build does not contain (`Versions`, ascending): an older build is deployed (a rollback, or a deployer built from an older commit), or migration files were deleted from the project. Checked on every deployment, before anything is changed; nothing ran | DbLive does not roll back a database: to roll back a release, roll back the application and keep the database (Section 18.8); deploy the newer build again. Restore deleted migration files |
| `DatabaseRequiresNewerDbLiveException: The database requires DbLive <version> or newer: a newer DbLive changed the dblive tables in a way older versions cannot read. ...` | A newer DbLive has deployed the database, and the minimum DbLive version stored there (`RequiredVersion`, Section 15) is above the one this DbLive works with (`MinCompatibleVersion`): an older build deployed again, by mistake or as the rollback of a release that upgraded DbLive. `DeployAsync` and `RunAllTestsAsync` check it before anything is changed; nothing ran | To roll back a release, roll back the application and keep the database (Section 18.8). Otherwise update the DbLive packages of the build to `RequiredVersion` or newer |
| `UndoNotSupportedException: <path> is an undo script. DbLive does not support undo scripts ...` | A file of `Migrations` whose second name part is `undo` or `u` (`005.undo.sql`, `005.u.sql`, `005.undo.settings.json`). Nothing ran | Delete the file (`RelativePath`). DbLive has no undo scripts: roll back the application, fix a wrong migration with a new migration (Section 18.8) |
| `MigrationDeploymentException` | SQL error in a migration/breaking script, or its command timeout. The message names the file and contains the provider's SQL error (number and line, or SqlState and position); for an error that does not come from the server it contains the message of the `DbLiveSqlException` instead (a timeout: `Execution Timeout Expired` on SQL Server, `Timeout during reading attempt` on PostgreSQL). The inner exception is the `DbLiveSqlException`, with the provider's exception inside it | Fix the script; for a timeout raise `MigrationTimeout` or the item's `Timeout`. It is not marked `applied`: in a transaction it was rolled back; with `TransactionWrapLevel: None` it may be partly applied and runs again from the start (Section 5.3) |
| `CodeDeploymentAggregateException` | A code file failed `MaxCodeDeployRetries` times, or once when the deployment transaction ended under it (`TransactionWrapLevel: Deployment`): on SQL Server a run-time error with `XACT_ABORT ON`, a failed conversion, a deadlock; on both providers a broken connection (the inner exception is the provider's error) or `DeploymentTimeout` (the inner exception is `TransactionException` with `TimeoutException` inside) | Read the inner exceptions; check dependencies and syntax. In the deployment transaction order dependencies with `CodeSubFoldersDeploymentOrder`; on SQL Server leave `set xact_abort on` out of code files; for `TimeoutException` raise `DeploymentTimeout` |
| `CodeDeploymentException: Deploy code breaking script error. File path: ...` | A breaking script of the Code folder failed (Section 6.1); the scripts after it did not run | Read the inner SQL error, fix the script (make it idempotent: `if exists`), run the breaking deployment again |
| `FolderDeploymentException: Error deploying <path> file.` | SQL error in a BeforeDeploy or AfterDeploy script, or its command timeout (Section 7); the scripts after it did not run. The message names the file (also in `RelativePath`) and contains the provider's SQL error, or the message of the `DbLiveSqlException` for an error that does not come from the server. The inner exception is the `DbLiveSqlException`. DbLive 1.5 and older threw the `DbLiveSqlException` itself, without the file | Fix the script and keep it idempotent: it runs again on the next deployment. For a timeout raise `BeforeDeployFolderTimeout` / `AfterDeployFolderTimeout` |
| `CodeNotDeployedException: Breaking changes are deployed only after the normal deployment of the same build, but N code file(s) are not deployed ...` | The breaking phase started while code files of this build are not deployed with their current content: the `Default` run of this build failed or did not run yet, or another build was deployed after it (Section 5.5). Nothing breaking ran. Its absence does not prove that `Default` succeeded: a build that added or changed no code file passes the guard anyway | Deploy the same build with `DeployParameters.Default` (fix the failed code file first), then the breaking deployment. Never work around it by deploying breaking from another build |
| `BreakingScriptMatchesTestPatternException` | A file of `Code/` is named like a breaking script and matches `TestFilePatterns` (`test.breaking.sql`, `t.b.sql`) | Rename it: `<name>.breaking.sql` for a breaking script, `<name>.test.sql` for a test |
| `SchemaChangedException` (deployment test only) | The second breaking deployment changed the schema: a breaking script of the Code folder or a BeforeDeploy/AfterDeploy script changes the schema when it runs again. The message lists the objects (Section 13.3) | Make the second run a no-op (`drop ... if exists`; do not test an object the script itself drops later in the same script) |
| `UnitTestsFailedException` | One or more SQL tests failed in `RunAllTestsAsync` | `FailedTests` lists the failed files; details are in the logs and `dblive.unit_test_run`. The deployment was a separate call and stays committed |
| `DatabaseNotDeployedException: The database has no DbLive tables ...` | `RunAllTestsAsync` against a database the project was never deployed to, or a wrong connection string | Deploy the project first (Section 8.2), or fix the connection string |
| `ScriptPathsDifferOnlyByCaseException: Files '<path>' and '<path>' differ only by case` | Two files of the project have relative paths that differ only by case (possible on Linux), in any folder, also `.txt`/`.md` files; DbLive identifies files ignoring case (Section 4) | Rename or delete one of the two files (or folders) |
| `FilesOutsideProjectFoldersException: N file(s) of the scripts folder are outside the project folders, so they would never be deployed: ...` | A file is outside `Migrations`, `Code`, `Tests`, `BeforeDeploy`, `AfterDeploy` (or the folders named in `settings.json`) and is not `settings.json` in the root: another folder (`PostDeployment/`), a misspelled `setting.json`, a `README.md` in the root (Section 4) | Rename the folder to a project folder (or set its name in `settings.json`, for example `"AfterDeployFolder": "PostDeployment"`), or move the files out of the scripts root |
| `FileNotUtf8Exception: File '<path>' of <folder or dll> is not UTF-8. ...` | A file of the project (a script, an item settings file, `settings.json`) has bytes that are not UTF-8: it is saved in Windows-1252, Windows-1251 or another ANSI code page without a BOM (Section 4). A file the deployment runs fails when the project is loaded, and nothing ran; a test file fails when the tests are read. DbLive 1.x deployed such a file with `�` in place of each non-ASCII character | Save the file as UTF-8, converting from the encoding it was written in. A migration or breaking script that is already applied: Section 18.2 |
| `DuplicateMigrationItemException` | Two files with the same version and type | Renumber the newer file (only if not applied anywhere) |
| `MigrationItemMustExistsException` | Breaking/settings without a migration for that version | Add the migration file or fix the version. To drop an old version of a code object, use a breaking script of the Code folder instead (Section 6.1) |
| `ObsoleteMigrationSettingsFileException` | Old per-version `<version>.settings.json` / `<version>.s.json` | Rename to `<version>.migration.settings.json` (the message names it); add `.breaking.settings.json` if the breaking script needs settings too; rename the key `MigrationTimeout` to `Timeout` |
| `MigrationSettingsWithoutScriptException` | `<version>.breaking.settings.json` without its script | Add the script or delete the settings file |
| `InvalidMigrationItemSettingsException` | Item settings file with an unknown key (also `MigrationTimeout`), invalid JSON, or `"TransactionWrapLevel": "Deployment"` | Section 9.3: keys `TransactionWrapLevel` (`Migration`/`None`), `TransactionIsolationLevel`, `Timeout` |
| `InvalidMigrationVersionException` | Version is not digits only (also a file such as `config.json` or a macOS `._001.migration.sql` in Migrations), or not `yyyyMMddHHmmss` with `EnforceTimestampVersion` | Rename or move the file |
| `UnknownMigrationSettingsException` | Unexpected `.json` file in Migrations | Rename to `<version>.<item>.settings.json` (`migration`/`breaking`) or move it |
| `NotSupportedTransactionIsolationLevelException` | `Snapshot` on PostgreSQL, in `settings.json` as `TransactionIsolationLevel` or `TestsTransactionIsolationLevel` (at the start of the deployment and of `RunAllTestsAsync`) or in an item settings file (at the start of the deployment; the message names the file) | Choose another level |
| `TransactionAbortedException` | A transaction ran longer than its timeout setting (`MigrationTimeout` or the item's `Timeout`, `DeploymentTimeout`, `UnitTestItemTimeout`; Section 10). The same value is the command timeout of each statement, so one long statement usually fails first with the provider's timeout error, as `MigrationDeploymentException` (`Execution Timeout Expired` on SQL Server, `Timeout during reading attempt` on PostgreSQL) | Raise that timeout (for one script: `Timeout` in its item settings file). `TransactionWrapLevel: None` removes only the transaction timeout, not the command timeout |
| `JsonException: The JSON property 'DowngradeTimeout' could not be mapped` reading `settings.json` | `DowngradeTimeout` was removed | Delete the key |
| SQL Server: `Incorrect syntax near 'GO'` in a test | `GO` in a test file | Remove `GO`; move setup into `setup.test.sql` |
| Test: `... looks like an assert result set, but its first column ...` | The assert column is misspelled or has no alias | Name it `assert`: `select 'rows' as assert` |
| Test: `Expected N result set(s), but M received.` | A `rows` / `rows-with-schema` test returns more or fewer result sets than it expects, often extra output in Arrange | Remove the extra output, or add the missing expected result set (Section 8.3) |

---

## 18. Recipes

### 18.1 Add DbLive to a new solution
With the template, one command does steps 1-4:

```bash
dotnet new install DbLive.Templates
dotnet new dblive -n MyDb --provider mssql       # or --provider postgresql; default mssql
```

It creates the folder `MyDb/` (or the `-o` folder) with:

| Created | Content |
|---|---|
| `MyDb.slnx` | Both projects. |
| `MyDb/` | Layout A (Section 3.2), `net10.0`, `<DbLiveScriptsFolder>Scripts</DbLiveScriptsFolder>`, references the provider package. `Program.cs`: the deployer for a local database, `DeployParameters.Default with { CreateDbIfNotExists = true }` (remove `CreateDbIfNotExists` before deploying to production, rule 18). `Scripts/settings.json`: `ProjectId` = the name in lower case. `Scripts/Migrations/<yyyyMMddHHmmss>.users.sql` (UTC time of creation): a users table with a check constraint on the name. `Scripts/Code/`: SQL Server `dbo.GetUser.sql` + `dbo.GetUser.test.sql`, PostgreSQL `get_user.sql` (a function) + `get_user.test.sql`. `Scripts/Tests/user-name-is-required.sql`: a data rule test without an assert. |
| `MyDb.Tests/` | xUnit v2, references `MyDb`, `DbLive.xunit` and `DbLive.Testcontainers.MSSQL` (or `.PostgreSQL`). `SqlTests.cs`: `SqlTestFixture` on the container builder (13.1) and the `[SqlFact]` class (13.2). `DeploymentTests.cs`: the `[SqlDeployFact]` class (13.3). |

- `-n` is used as it is for the folders, project files, `Assembly.Load("<name>")` and the SQL Server database name in `Program.cs`; the PostgreSQL database name and the `ProjectId` take it in lower case; namespaces take the identifier form (`Contoso.Billing-Db` → `Contoso.Billing_Db.Tests`). Without `-n`, the name of the output folder.
- `dotnet test` in the solution folder runs 3 tests (2 SQL test files and the deployment test); Docker must be running. `dotnet run --project MyDb` deploys to the local database of `Program.cs`.
- The example scripts can be changed or deleted until a migration is deployed to a database that is kept (rule 1); the test databases are dropped. Version new migrations with timestamps too (Section 5.1): a lower version such as `002` would run before the example migration on a new database.

Without the template:
1. Create the SQL project (class library or console app) with a `Scripts` folder. Its `.csproj` sets `<DbLiveScriptsFolder>Scripts</DbLiveScriptsFolder>` and references the provider (layout A) or `DbLive` (layout B), which embeds the folder (3.1); add no other DbLive items to the `.csproj`.
2. Create `Scripts/Migrations/<yyyyMMddHHmmss>.<name>.sql` with the first change, and `Scripts/settings.json` with `ProjectId` (rule 17), optionally `"EnforceTimestampVersion": true`.
3. Create the deployer (3.3).
4. Create the xUnit test project that references the SQL project, `DbLive.xunit` and `DbLive.Testcontainers.MSSQL` (or `DbLive.Testcontainers.PostgreSQL`), with a one-line fixture on `MsSqlContainerFixtureBuilder` (13.1) and the `[SqlFact]` and `[SqlDeployFact]` classes (Section 13).

### 18.2 Add DbLive to an existing database (brownfield)
DbLive has no baseline command. Recommended approach:
1. First migration = a baseline that is safe on the existing database **and** builds a new empty one: guard every object (`if object_id('dbo.Users','U') is null create table ...` / `create table if not exists ...`).
2. Script existing procedures, functions and views into `Code/` as `create or alter` / `create or replace`. They are re-applied on the first deployment.
3. Save every file as UTF-8 (Section 4). Scripts written in an old editor or taken from samples are often in the ANSI code page of the machine (Windows-1252, Windows-1251) and fail with `FileNotUtf8Exception`. Convert each from the encoding it was written in (`iconv -f WINDOWS-1252 -t UTF-8`, or "Reopen with Encoding" and then "Save with Encoding" in VS Code), and check its non-ASCII characters afterwards.
4. Deploy to a copy of production first, then to production. The `dblive` schema is added; existing tables are untouched.

A file that is not UTF-8 and that DbLive 1.x deployed fails with `FileNotUtf8Exception` after the upgrade. DbLive 1.x read each of its non-ASCII characters as `�` (`U+FFFD`) and deployed that text:
- A code file, a BeforeDeploy or AfterDeploy script, a test, a settings file, or a migration not applied yet: convert it to UTF-8. A code file then has a new hash and is deployed again, with the right text.
- A migration or breaking script that is applied: converting it changes its text (`�` becomes `é`), so the next deployment fails with `MigrationChecksumMismatchException` (Section 5.4). Either save it as UTF-8 with the text DbLive 1.x read, which keeps the hash: `pwsh -c '$p = "Scripts/Migrations/001.status.sql"; [IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, [IO.File]::ReadAllText($p))'` (PowerShell 7 decodes like DbLive and writes UTF-8 without a BOM; the `�` characters stay in the file). Or convert it properly and deploy once with `RepairMigrationChecksums = true`. Either way, the rows the migration wrote hold `�`: fix them with a new migration.

### 18.3 Add a table
`Migrations/<v>.create-orders.sql` with `create table ...`. Add a procedure in `Code/` and a test next to it.

### 18.4 Add a column (no downtime)
Migration: add a nullable column, or a non-null column with a default. Update procedures in `Code/` (new version name if the contract changes). The previous application keeps working: it does not know the column.

### 18.5 Rename or move a column (expand/contract)
1. Migration v: add the new column/table, backfill it, add a temporary trigger that keeps old and new in sync.
2. Code: new procedure versions (`..._v2`) use the new structure; old versions keep working.
3. Breaking v: drop the sync trigger and the old column. Drop the old procedure versions in breaking scripts next to their files (Section 6.1); they run before the migration breaking scripts, so a view or function of the old version that reads the old column is gone before the column is dropped.
4. Release: deploy `Default` → deploy the new app → drain the old app → deploy `Breaking`. Until `Breaking` runs, the previous application works on the new schema, so a rollback is a rollback of the application (Section 18.8). Run `Breaking` only when the release is confirmed.

### 18.6 Change a procedure's contract
Rename the object in its file (`GetUser_v1` → `GetUser_v2`), update the test file, and create (or extend) the breaking script next to the file: `Code/dbo/GetUser.breaking.sql` with `drop proc if exists dbo.GetUser_v1;` (PostgreSQL: `drop function if exists get_user_v1(int);`). No migration is needed. Always `if exists`: the script runs on every breaking deployment (Section 6.1). When `_v3` replaces `_v2` later, replace the content with the drop of `_v2`; keeping the old drops is harmless. Do not put the drop into AfterDeploy (Section 7), and do not create a migration version only to carry the drop. If only the implementation changes and the contract stays the same, keep the name and just edit the file.

### 18.7 Long-running index / data backfill
Own migration version with `<v>.migration.settings.json` `{ "TransactionWrapLevel": "None", "Timeout": "01:00:00" }`. Why: a transaction holds every lock until the migration commits, so the touched tables are blocked for the whole migration; without it each statement commits and releases its locks, and the database stays online. SQL Server: `with (online = on)`. PostgreSQL: `create index concurrently if not exists ...`, alone in its file. Make it re-runnable (`if not exists (select * from sys.indexes where name = ...)`), because a failure leaves it partially applied and the next deployment runs the whole script again. On PostgreSQL a failed or cancelled concurrent build leaves an invalid index (`pg_index.indisvalid = false`, PostgreSQL behavior), and `if not exists` skips it on the next run: the deployment succeeds and the index stays invalid (unused by queries, updated on writes). DbLive does not check index validity. Next to the migration, add a BeforeDeploy script that drops the index by name if it is invalid; BeforeDeploy runs on every deployment before the migrations, so after a failure the next deployment drops the index and the migration builds it again:
```sql
-- BeforeDeploy/drop-invalid-ix_users_name.sql
do $$
begin
  if exists (select from pg_index where indexrelid = to_regclass('ix_users_name') and not indisvalid) then
    drop index ix_users_name;
  end if;
end $$;
```
Not in the migration file: with a second statement the file is one implicit transaction, `create index concurrently` fails with `25001` and the `drop` is rolled back. Not `drop index concurrently`: in a `do` block it fails with `25001: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot be executed from a function`; the plain `drop index` takes a short exclusive lock on the table. By name only: an index that another session is building concurrently is invalid too. The script is idempotent (BeforeDeploy rule 6); remove it once every database has the index. A breaking script that drops an index online/concurrently needs its own `<v>.breaking.settings.json` `{ "TransactionWrapLevel": "None" }`; the migration's settings file does not apply to it.

Batch large updates, in their own version with `TransactionWrapLevel: None`, re-runnable (each batch picks the rows not done yet). SQL Server: a `while` loop of `update top (n) ...`; each statement commits on its own. PostgreSQL: a file with several statements is one implicit transaction (Section 16), so the batches must commit themselves: a `do` block with `commit` after each batch (or `call` of a procedure that does it), alone in its file:
```sql
do $$
declare n int;
begin
  loop
    update users set active = true
    where user_id in (select user_id from users where active is null limit 10000);
    get diagnostics n = row_count;
    exit when n = 0;
    commit;
  end loop;
end $$;
```

### 18.8 Roll back a release
DbLive has no undo scripts and does not roll back a database. Roll a release back this way:

- **Before the breaking phase: roll back the application, keep the database.** Migrations only add (rule 4, expand/contract), so the previous application runs on the new schema; the old versions of code objects (`GetUser_v1`) are still there, because DbLive never drops code and only the breaking phase drops them. The database serves both versions. Do not deploy the previous build of the database: its project lacks the new migration versions, so it fails with `DatabaseAheadOfProjectException` and changes nothing (Section 5.2).
- **A bug in a code object**: revert the file in git and deploy a new release (`Default`). Code is deployed by state: the reverted file's hash differs, so it runs and the old version of the object is back; a file the release had deleted runs again when it comes back, because its row is `removed` (Section 6). A code-only release (no new migration version, and no DbLive upgrade that raised the minimum DbLive version) can also be rolled back by deploying the previous build, which redeploys its code. Never run the breaking phase of the newer build afterwards: its guard does not see this case when the newer build only deleted code files (Section 5.5).
- **A wrong migration**: fix it with a new migration version. Never edit or delete an applied one (rules 1 and 2).
- **A release that upgraded DbLive**: when the release notes of the new DbLive version say that older versions can no longer deploy the database, the previous build fails with `DatabaseRequiresNewerDbLiveException` and changes nothing (Section 15), also when the release has no migrations of its own. Roll back the application, keep the database; the next release of the old code needs the newer DbLive packages. A deployment of the new build that failed on an error in its project files (an undo script left in the project, a file outside the project folders, a wrong file name: Sections 4 and 5.1) changed nothing on the server, so the previous build still deploys the database (Section 12, step 1).
- **The breaking phase is the point of no return.** It drops what the previous application uses. Run it only when the release is confirmed, and never for a release whose application was rolled back: no guard sees that case, because the code of the release is still deployed (Section 5.5). After the breaking phase, fix forward with a new release, or restore a backup.

Why there are no undo scripts: before the breaking phase the database needs no rollback; after it an undo would restore the structure, not the data the breaking scripts dropped; an undo of a migration would drop the data written since it ran. An undo file left in a project fails the deployment with `UndoNotSupportedException` (Section 5.1).

### 18.9 Someone edited an applied migration
Preferred: revert the file to its applied content (git history) and add a new version with the intended change. If the edit is cosmetic and the database already matches: deploy once with `RepairMigrationChecksums = true`.

### 18.10 CI/CD pipeline
1. Build.
2. `dotnet test` (Testcontainers): runs `[SqlDeployFact]` (release, breaking phase, breaking phase again with the schema check, all SQL tests) and `[SqlFact]` tests.
3. Deploy the database: `dotnet MyDb.Deploy.dll` with `DeployParameters.Default`. The deployer does not run the SQL tests (step 2 did).
4. Deploy the application; old and new versions run side by side.
5. Remove the old application.
6. Deploy breaking changes: `dotnet MyDb.Deploy.dll --breaking` (`DeployParameters.Breaking`), with the same build as step 3, once the release is confirmed. Run it only when step 3 succeeded for this build: if step 3 did not complete, it fails with `CodeNotDeployedException` only when the build added or changed a code file (Section 5.5). Up to this step a rollback is a rollback of the application (steps 4–5); after it, fix forward (Section 18.8).

Production settings (the defaults are the safe values, except `ProjectId`):
- `ProjectId` set in `settings.json` (rule 17, Section 14).
- `CreateDbIfNotExists = false` (default): the production database is created outside DbLive, and the deployer's login needs no permission to create databases (rule 18).
- `RepairMigrationChecksums = false` (default); `true` only for one deployment after checking that the database matches the files (Section 18.9).
- `MigrationChecksumMode: Strict` (default).
- `TransactionWrapLevel: Migration` (default); `None` in the item settings of a script that cannot run in a transaction (Section 18.7). Not `Deployment`: it holds locks for the whole deployment and deploys code single-threaded (Section 10).
- `MigrationTimeout` (default 12 hours) and `CodeItemTimeout` (default 30 seconds) as the release window allows; `Timeout` in the item settings of a longer migration script (Section 9.3).
- No `RunAllTestsAsync()` in the deployer (rule 12).

### 18.11 Local development loop
Run the xUnit tests: each `[SqlFact]` test can be run and debugged from Test Explorer, against a new database the fixture deploys. To work with a local database, run the deployer against it (`CreateDbIfNotExists = true`); it does not run the tests. The scripts are read from the SQL project's dll; Test Explorer, `dotnet test` and `dotnet run` build first, so edits are picked up on the next run.

---

## 19. Known limitations

- No CLI tool; deployments are started from your own C# code.
- With `SetProject`, scripts are read from the dll, so a changed script takes effect only after a build. Use `SetScriptsFolder` to deploy a folder without building.
- xUnit v2 only (`DbLive.xunit`).
- Code objects are never dropped automatically; drift made directly in the database is not detected.
- Supported engines: SQL Server / Azure SQL and PostgreSQL. SQLite and MySQL are planned.
